description: Export Bitbucket, Confluence and Jira history as tamper-evident evidence — read-only, verbatim payloads, sha256-manifested JSONL. For tax audits, legal holds and e-discovery.

readme.text:
# atlassian-evidence

**English** | [Tiếng Việt](README.vi.md)

**Export the full history of Confluence, Jira and Bitbucket Cloud as tamper-evident
evidence** — strictly read-only, verbatim payloads, every batch sha256-manifested.

*Trích xuất toàn bộ lịch sử Confluence / Jira / Bitbucket Cloud thành bằng chứng có thể kiểm
chứng, phục vụ giải trình thuế, kiểm toán và tranh chấp pháp lý —*
[đọc bản tiếng Việt](README.vi.md).

---

## Is this your problem?

A tax authority, an auditor, or opposing counsel asks you to prove that **a specific thing
happened at a specific time** — and the evidence is scattered across years of Jira,
Confluence and Bitbucket:

- *"Prove this R&D project was actually carried out during fiscal year 2019."*
- *"Produce the complete discussion behind this decision — no excerpts."*
- *"This document says it was edited on 12 March. Where is the version before the edit?"*
- Employment disputes, IP ownership claims, or a departing employee who deleted or rewrote
  data on the way out.

It sounds simple until you try it.

### Why the built-in exports are not enough

| Approach | Why it fails as evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Jira XML/CSV export | Drops changelog, worklogs, comments; reformats timestamps |
| Confluence PDF/Word export | Current version only — version history is what matters |
| Screenshots | Unverifiable, trivially challenged as edited |
| A repo you already cloned locally | Unpushed local commits contaminate the evidence |
| Atlassian full-site backup | Opaque format; you cannot verify or produce any single item from it |

The core problem: evidence must be **provably unaltered** and **verbatim** — not "data that a
tool has reinterpreted for you".

### How this tool solves it

- **Read-only, enforced structurally.** The HTTP client exposes exactly one method, `.get()` —
  POST/PUT/DELETE do not exist anywhere in the code. Git is restricted to `clone --mirror`,
  `fetch --prune` and `log`. There is no code path that can write back to the source systems.
- **Absolutely verbatim.** Raw API payloads are preserved in each record's `raw` field. Every
  timestamp is stored as **the exact string the source returned** and is never parsed into a
  `datetime` and re-formatted — that silently rewrites timezone and millisecond precision.
- **Verifiable.** Each closed JSONL batch is hashed into `manifest.jsonl`. Re-run `sha256sum`
  at any point to prove a file has not changed since extraction.
- **Complete history.** Confluence captures **every version** of every page, not just the
  latest. Jira captures issues plus comments, changelogs and worklogs. Bitbucket captures
  commits (both `author_date` and `committer_date`, read from git itself) and pull requests in
  every state.
- **Transparent scope.** Each run writes a scope report of what was covered, and every object
  that was denied or missing (403/404) is recorded in `errors.jsonl` — what you *could not*
  read is itself disclosable information, not something to quietly omit.
- **Survives long runs.** Per-stream cursors, and a batch is closed before its cursor advances.
  If the machine dies mid-run, re-issue the same command and it continues.

---

## Install

Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Python 3.14+.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zentrung/atlassian-evidence.git
cd atlassian-evidence
uv sync
```

## Configure

Create an API token at **id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens**, then export seven
variables. All are **required** — the tool deliberately defaults nothing, so it can never
point at the wrong tenant by accident:

```bash
export ATLASSIAN_SITE=your-company.atlassian.net   # no https:// prefix
export JIRA_USERNAME=you@company.com               # also used for Confluence
export JIRA_TOKEN=<api-token>

export BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE=your-workspace
export BITBUCKET_USER=you@company.com              # REST API: MUST be the email
export BITBUCKET_GIT_USER=your-bitbucket-username  # git clone: MUST be the username
export BITBUCKET_TOKEN=<api-token>
```

> **The trap that makes people give up:** Bitbucket Cloud needs **two different identities for
> the same token**. The REST API accepts only the **email** (a username returns 401 *"API token
> must be used with an atlassian registered email"*), while **git over HTTPS accepts only the
> username** (an email returns *"Authentication failed"*). Find your username via
> `GET /2.0/user` (field `username`), or in Bitbucket → Personal settings.

## Usage

```bash
uv run evidence extract --source all --output-dir ./raw   # full run; can take hours
uv run evidence status --output-dir ./raw                 # which streams are unfinished
uv run evidence extract --source jira --output-dir ./raw  # a single source
```

Stopping is always safe: `Ctrl-C` (or `pkill -INT -f '\.venv/bin/evidence extract'`), then
re-issue **the same command** to resume from where it stopped.

A completed stream is treated as a **snapshot of that moment**: re-runs skip it and will not
pick up activity that happened afterwards. Use a fresh `--output-dir` for a newer snapshot.

## Output

```
raw/
├── manifest.jsonl   # per closed batch: batch_id, record_count, sha256, run_id, window
├── errors.jsonl     # objects denied or missing (403/404) — the scope you could NOT read
├── README.md        # per-run scope report + fidelity caveats
├── .state/          # per-stream cursors
├── .mirrors/        # git mirror clones (see warning below)
└── {source}/{year}/batch-NNNNN.jsonl
```

Each JSONL line is one record sharing a common envelope: `source_system`, `object_type`, `id`,
`url`, `title`, `body_raw`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `author_account_id`, `container`, and
`raw` holding the complete original payload.

Verify integrity at any time:

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, hashlib, pathlib
for m in map(json.loads, open('raw/manifest.jsonl')):
    f = pathlib.Path(m['file'])
    if hashlib.sha256(f.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != m['sha256']:
        print('MISMATCH:', f)
print('verification complete')
EOF
```

## Important notes

- **Delete `raw/.mirrors/` before sharing the dataset.** Git mirrors store credentials in their
  own `config`. Safest habit: revoke the token as soon as extraction finishes.
- **Duplicates after a resume.** Interrupting mid-window and resuming can repeat records across
  batches. Deduplicate on `(source_system, object_type, id, version_number)`.
- **sha256 attests the extracted JSONL files**, not the original HTTP bytes.
- **`author_display_name` is the name at extraction time** (the APIs expose no historical
  names); `author_account_id` is the stable identifier.
- **Scope equals what the extracting account can see.** Permission-restricted content is
  invisible by construction and cannot be enumerated — use an account with sufficient access.
- **Confluence comments are latest-version only**; full version history applies to pages and
  blogposts.
- **Bitbucket repositories with many branches run for a long time with no log output** — the
  tool walks commits per branch over REST before writing the first record. Silence is not a
  hang.

## Development

```bash
uv run pytest -q
uv run ruff check --no-cache .
```
